summary: Two weeks, 70 messages, and the single most serious item on this account has still never been answered. On Aug 31 Lauren phoned Chase herself and reported two things in consecutive messages: "They said that the name ALTR mgmt LLC is not matching the name on the account even though the numbers are" and "And your account was flagged by Chase for fraud/scam transactions so they won’t send it through so they won’t send it even if I say so". Eleven days later not one ALTR person - not Stephski, not Ollie, not Derrek - has acknowledged the second sentence. She then closed the loop herself on Sep 4: after Stephski finally gave her the registered name, she compared it to the paperwork and wrote "Ahh okay the invoice says mgmt", followed by "I’ll try and wire for the rest of this last invoice". Stephski's entire response, twenty hours later, was "Okay perfect so sorry about that!!". No corrected invoice was issued in the seven days that followed, and no wire ever landed - she paid the whole thing in Zelle. The money still arrived, entirely through her effort. Invoice 2 settled Sep 2 in three daily $5k Zelles. Invoice 3 (period Aug 15-31, $21,126.95, issued Sep 1) was then paid down in four more $5k Zelles on Sep 3, Sep 7, Sep 9 and Sep 10 - "Sent another 5k so now still have 11,126.95 to go" - leaving $1,126.95 she committed to send on Sep 11. That is seven manual installments and two rejected wires in 21 days, all to work around a defect in ALTR's own banking. ALTR's contribution was to chase her for the next one: "Recieved! Can you shoot another one tomorrow?" (Sep 9), then "Let me know 🙂" three hours later. Derrek sent ZERO messages across the entire fourteen-day window and has now been silent since Aug 27 - fifteen days - through the fraud-flag disclosure, through a third invoice carrying the unevidenced 5% ads fee, and through 41 days of promised phone-farm updates. Ollie sent four messages in fourteen days and all four were requests of her: follow this fan (Aug 30), where are the new pictures (Sep 4), snap add mattie_1712 (Sep 7), thank you (Sep 7). Not one of his six open items moved; the livestream he personally built a subscriber poll for is now 21 days dead. The one genuine bright spot is Mayson. He escalated her unanswered banking question on Sep 3, then on Sep 4 proactively opened the trial-reel conversation she first asked about on Jul 11 - "would you be available for a quick call on Monday to discuss a brand new feature for posting trial reels on instagram more effectively?" - got a call booked and held on Sep 5, and by Sep 10 had opened a second promo funnel on Snapchat with a drive and admin request. That is the first unprompted growth initiative this account has received in over a month, and it came from a queue-account chatter, not from account management. Michelle delivered the weekly leak report on Sep 1 and Sep 8, unchased, weeks seven and eight unbroken since Jul 17.

health.rationale: Down 2 from 51 across a two-week window. The scoreboard is split in a way that should worry the owner more than a single low number would. Client conduct is close to perfect: 36 messages, seven Zelle installments totalling $27,103 across two invoices, every ask answered within hours, and an apology offered to ALTR for a delay ALTR caused. Service delivery is worse than last period, not better. The Chase fraud flag on ALTR MANAGEMENT LLC has now sat unacknowledged for 11 days. The client herself identified the invoice defect on Sep 4 ("Ahh okay the invoice says mgmt") and was told "Okay perfect so sorry about that!!" - seven days later there is still no corrected invoice, and the wire she said she would attempt never went through, so she is on manual installments indefinitely. Stephski's only proactive messages in the back half of the window were chases for the next installment. Derrek sent nothing at all in fourteen days. Ollie sent four messages, all asks, while six items aged past 20, 21, 24, 27, 35 and 40 days. The only reason this is not in the low 40s is Mayson: he escalated her ignored question, then opened the trial-reel feature and a Snapchat funnel unprompted, and she engaged immediately ("Yes I’d like to get those cranking"). She is still leaning in. That will not last if the fourth invoice arrives with the same wrong beneficiary name and the same 5% ads line with nothing behind it.
